sources.entry: mempalace — Memory-oriented tooling for AI agents, focused on persistent context, recall, and more structured long-term memory behavior.

summary.one_liner: MemPalace is a local-first AI memory system that stores conversation history and project content verbatim and retrieves it with semantic search, with no API calls required for the core path.
summary.what_it_does: MemPalace stores conversation history as verbatim text and retrieves it via semantic search without summarizing or paraphrasing. Content is organized into wings (people and projects), rooms (topics), and drawers (original content) so searches can be scoped. The retrieval layer is pluggable, with ChromaDB as the default and additional local and server backends such as sqlite_exact, rust_exact, milvus, qdrant, and pgvector. It ships a CLI (mine, search, wake-up, audit, sweep) and an MCP server with 47 tools covering palace reads and writes, a temporal knowledge graph backed by local SQLite, agent diaries, and agent coordination. Auto-save hooks are documented for Claude Code, Codex CLI, and Cursor IDE. The README reports 96.6% R@5 raw recall on LongMemEval with no LLM, plus additional benchmark figures.
use_cases: give an AI coding agent persistent memory across sessions
search past Claude Code or Codex conversation history
store and semantically search project files for later recall
run a private local memory store with no cloud calls
share a memory hub across a team via a server deployment
track entities and relationships over time in a local knowledge graph
how_to_run: mempalace search "why did we switch to GraphQL"
notable: Verbatim storage with no summarization; retrieval scoped by wings, rooms, and drawers
Pluggable storage backend contract with multiple local and server options
Reports 96.6% R@5 raw on LongMemEval with no LLM or API key
Temporal knowledge graph with validity windows, backed by local SQLite
Optional OpenAI-compatible embedding endpoint for local or LAN servers
caveats: Native Termux installation is unsupported; Android ARM64 users must use a Debian PRoot container
The GPU Docker image is x86_64-only and is not published, so it must be built locally
The README warns of impostor domains and says only the GitHub repo, PyPI package, and mempalaceofficial.com are official
